one_liner: Zstd-backed lossless RGB/RGBA image format that encodes about 23x and decodes 4.6x faster than libpng, with smaller files.
what_it_does: Zpng turns an interleaved pixel buffer (1 to 8 bytes per pixel) into its own container: an 8-byte header (magic 0xFBF8, 16-bit width and height, channel count, bytes per channel) followed by a single zstd frame. The API is three C functions: ZPNG_Compress(const ZPNG_ImageData*) returns a malloc'd ZPNG_Buffer, ZPNG_Decompress(ZPNG_Buffer) returns a ZPNG_ImageData, and ZPNG_Free releases either buffer. It does not read or write PNG and has no metadata, streaming or row-by-row API. The bundled CLI loads images with stb_image and writes PNG output with stb_image_write.
how_it_is_fast: Filtering is one pass per row: each byte is replaced by its difference from the same channel of the pixel to the left (PNG's Sub filter only, with no Up or Paeth filters and no per-row filter search). For 8-bit RGB and RGBA it then applies the reversible GB-RG colour transform from BCIF (Y=B, U=G-B, V=G-R on the residuals) and writes Y, U, V and alpha as separate planes. In the author's README experiments the plane split made output about 1.8% smaller and compression faster than interleaved data. The planar residual buffer then goes through one ZSTD_compress call at level 1 (zstd's fast match finder with Huffman and FSE entropy coding). libpng at its defaults instead tries every filter on each row and runs zlib deflate at the default level. Decoding is ZSTD_decompress followed by the inverse transform. There are no SIMD intrinsics; the loops rely on compiler auto-vectorization (its CMake Release flags are -O3 -march=native).
when_to_use: Caching, storing or moving 8-bit RGB or RGBA frames between programs you control (capture tools, asset caches, dataset shards), where a private format is acceptable: 126 MPixels/s encode and 256 MPixels/s decode on one i5-10210U thread across the QOI suite.

Photographs and photo textures, where it gives the smallest files among the fast codecs in the QOIR table: photo_kodak CmpRatio 0.4776 (libpng 0.5630, QOIR 0.5345, QOI 0.5829) and textures_photo 0.4156 (libpng 0.5977, QOIR 0.6052).
Read-heavy pipelines: decoding (256 MPixels/s) runs about twice as fast as encoding and beats QOI (193.5) and libjxl's fast-lossless path (33.2 decode) in the same harness.
Projects that already link zstd and want a lossless image codec of roughly 600 lines under BSD-3-Clause that they can vendor and adapt.
when_not_to_use: Interchange or long-term archives: .zpng is not PNG, no viewer or browser reads it, the header has no version field and is written in host byte order.
Untrusted files: the decoder trusts the header and never checks that zstd filled the output (see gotchas). Treat it as unsafe on hostile input unless you add those checks.
Images wider or taller than 65535 px: width and height are stored as uint16_t, and ZPNG_Compress truncates them with no error. The QOIR adapter adds the missing guard itself.

16-bit data: deltas are taken per byte, not per 16-bit sample, and the colour transform runs only on 8-bit RGB/RGBA. ZPNG_Decompress also reports StrideBytes as width x channels, half the real stride. The CLI loads with stbi_load, which converts 16-bit PNGs to 8-bit (issue #6, closed with no fix in the code).

Flat graphics and icons, or when you need the smallest output: on QOIR's icon_512 set Zpng is larger than libpng (CmpRatio 0.0534 vs 0.0499), and on textures_pk it is larger than QOIR (0.5384 vs 0.4929). WebP lossless (0.1651) and slower JPEG XL settings are much smaller overall. Encoding small icons is also slower (icon_64: 80.8 MPixels/s).

integration.form: source-drop (zpng.cpp + zpng.h), or the CMake zpnglib static library, which also compiles the vendored zstd
integration.dependencies: zstd (a copy of zstd 1.3.4 is vendored in zstd/; the QOIR harness links the system libzstd instead, so newer versions work); the CLI and test app also use stb_image and stb_image_write
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 11), CMake 3.5; the API is extern "C", but zpng.cpp uses templates and must be compiled as C++
integration.platforms: Any (portable scalar C++, no intrinsics); the CMake Release flags hard-code -O3 -march=native on non-MSVC compilers, which ties binaries to the build machine's CPU; files are not portable between little- and big-endian hosts because the header is written as a raw struct
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. From reading the code there is no global state and every call allocates its own buffers and zstd context, so concurrent calls on separate buffers look safe.

gotchas: Possible memory-safety bug on crafted input (found by reading the code; not run): ZPNG_Decompress computes byteCount = width x height x bytesPerPixel in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic with no overflow check. A header of 32768 x 32768 RGBA wraps the product to 0, and with an empty zstd frame UnpackAndUnfilter then reads and writes about 4 GiB past two zero-byte allocations. The decoder also ignores how many bytes ZSTD_decompress actually produced, and level-1 frames carry no checksum, so truncated or corrupted files decode silently to zero-filled pixels.
ZPNG_Compress ignores the input StrideBytes and assumes tightly packed rows; padded or sub-image buffers come out scrambled with no error.

Memory per call is about 2-3x the image: compression allocates a filtered copy plus a ZSTD_compressBound output buffer, and decompression allocates the packed buffer plus the output. Results come back in malloc'd buffers that you must release with ZPNG_Free.

The README's 'less than 6% of the time of a PNG compressor and 66% of the size' compares against stb_image_write's stbi_write_png, not libpng (apps/zpng_app.cpp times the stbi_write_png call, which also writes the 41.9 MB file to disk), against an in-memory Zpng compress of one JPEG-derived photo. The independent QOIR numbers are the ones to rely on.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Zpng over QOI or QOIR when file size matters more than the last bit of speed: on the QOI suite its output is about 14% smaller than QOIR's (0.2182 vs 0.2525) and 23% smaller than QOI's (0.2823), at about 75% of QOIR's encode speed (126 vs 169 MPixels/s) and similar decode speed (256 vs 276). Pick fpng or fpnge when you need real PNG files. libjxl fast_lossless matches Zpng's size (0.2171) in a standard format but decodes about 7.7x slower (33.16 vs 256.32 MPixels/s).
verified_claims_summary: Nigel Tao's QOIR harness ran single-threaded on an Intel i5-10210U with gcc 10.2.1 (-O3 -march=native for the adapter), 5 repetitions per image, over the whole QOI benchmark suite. Zpng (the vendored zpng.cpp with the system libzstd at level 1) encoded 126.21 MPixels/s and decoded 256.32 MPixels/s, against 5.49 and 56.18 for Debian Bullseye's libpng at default settings (about 23x and 4.6x, derived from page data), at CmpRatio 0.2182 vs 0.2423. The WangXuan95 CLIC2021 shootout used a lightly modified catid build (PNM output and a level switch; g++ -static -O3, vendored zstd 1.3.4) against Pillow's PNG, with process startup included in the times.
status_note: Abandoned since 2018-06-17 (one PR, #4 from 2018, now closed; issue #5 on integer-type portability is still open), but BSD-3-Clause and about 600 lines, so it is easy to vendor; add header and decompressed-size checks before you feed it files you did not write.
